title: telemetry-bridge-forensics-scratchpad
content:
Context and purpose:
- Personal forensic notes for the recent telemetry regressions (metrics drop + partial traces missing + delayed logs).
- Goal: capture commands tried, raw snippets, timelines and hypotheses so we can hand off to SRE or use in a postmortem.
- Not official timeline — rough notes while reproducing in staging.

TL;DR summary (what I saw)
- Around 2026-02-24 18:10 UTC, customer-facing ingress in eu-west started showing reduced trace coverage (sampling rate appears intact in control plane but spans lost between api-gateway -> frontend-proxy).
- Logs from downstream services arrive in Loki with 10–30s ingestion delays, and some batches drop entirely (gap windows).
- Metrics (request_count, latency_p99) reporting to Prometheus exporter shows 30% lower cardinality for a subset of instrumented labels (route, model).
- Tracing agent (obs-agent v1.12.0) on k8s nodes shows restart churn on 2026-02-24 17:55–18:05 UTC with SIGTERM due to liveness probe timeouts.

Initial reproduction steps I ran (staging cluster)
- scaled up a noisy client generator to 600rps targeted at /v1/generate and /v1/embed routes.
- kubectl commands and checks:
  - kubectl -n observability get pods -l app=obs-agent -o wide
  - kubectl -n observability logs obs-agent-5k7p -c obs-agent --since=1h | sed -n '1,200p'
  - kubectl -n gateway describe pod frontend-proxy-2 | grep -i "Readiness\|Liveness" -A3

Key commands and outputs (snippets)
- obs-agent logs showing repeated warnings:
  "2026-02-24T17:56:12Z WARN agent::pipeline::sender: upstream write failed: write tcp 10.2.3.4:4150->10.9.64.8:443: write: connection reset by peer"
  "2026-02-24T17:56:13Z INFO agent::liveness: health check timed out after=15s"
- system journal on node-12:
  "Mar 24 17:56:14 node-12 systemd[1]: obs-agent.service: Failed with result 'signal'."
- tcpdump during a failure window (filtered):
  "17:56:12.123456 IP node-12.45678 > collector-eu-west.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0"
  "17:56:12.456789 IP collector-eu-west.443 > node-12.45678: Flags [R.], seq 1, ack 1, win 0, length 0"

Quick grep across logs (what's missing)
- grep for trace ids from gateway (trace ID 0x9af3e) shows spans in api-gateway and in frontend-proxy but NOT in model-serving pods.
- model-serving logs show no incoming request for some sample traces that exist in the gateway logs -> suggests loss between proxy and model-serving or agent not forwarding spans.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Obs-agent outbound TLS connections to the collector were intermittently reset by upstream (collector-side scaling / conn limit / firewall). Symptoms: TCP RST seen repeatedly; bunched timeouts cause liveness to fail and agent restarts, losing transient span buffer.
2) Backpressure in the local forwarder queue: when a spike occurs, buffer size fills and samples get dropped before flush. Agent config changed recently: batch_size lowered from 64->32 and retry_backoff reduced.
3) Sidecar proxy (istio) mTLS or egress policy intermittently rejecting connections to collector IPs due to recent Cilium egress policy rollout in eu-west.
4) Prometheus exporter scrape jobs changed relabeling, causing label cardinality shrink (not an agent issue but a scrape/config mismatch).

Commands and inspections to validate each hypothesis
- Check collector/relay health & connection limits
  - curl -sS https://collector.internal/ehealth | jq .  # shows active_conn_count, max_conn=2000
  - kubectl -n observability get deploy obs-collector -o yaml | yq '.spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources'
- Inspect agent config on node (mounted config map)
  - kubectl -n observability exec -it obs-agent-5k7p -- cat /etc/obs/agent.yaml | sed -n '1,160p'
  - look for: max_buffer_bytes, batch_size, retry_backoff_ms, tls:enable, tls:ca_file
- Check Cilium egress policy changes around that time
  - kubectl -n kube-system get cnp -o wide --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 20
  - kubectl -n kube-system describe cnp allow-collector-egress
- Prometheus relabel check
  - curl -s http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/targets?state=active | jq '.data.activeTargets[] | select(.labels.job=="obs-exporter")'

Findings so far (evidence correlating to hypotheses)
- Collector shows spikes in active_conn_count around 17:55–18:02 UTC, close to the observed window. max_conn=1024. There are sustained short bursts where active_conn reaches ~980.
- obs-agent config on nodes shows batch_size: 32 and max_buffer_bytes: 1e6 (1MB). Previous deploy notes show we intended 4MB.
- Cilium logs show a policy rollout at 17:50 UTC that added an egress rate-limit/connection threshold for the eu-west nodepool (policy id cnp-2026-02-24-3). The policy contains "toPorts: port: 443, toEndpoints: collector" directive.
- Prometheus relabel change was committed earlier in Feb but affected only the exporter job that runs on dedicated infra; not likely root cause for missing traces.

Immediate mitigations executed in staging (notes)
- Increased obs-agent max_buffer_bytes to 4e6 and batch_size back to 64 via configmap patch, then rolled agents with rolling restart: kubectl -n observability rollout restart daemonset/obs-agent
- Temporarily added an egress allow policy exception for collector host in Cilium (policy rollback) to rule out policy mismatches.
- Collector scaling: patch replica count from 3 -> 6 to increase connection headroom.

Observed after mitigation
- Trace coverage recovered gradually over ~7 minutes after agent restarts and buffer increases. No more immediate RSTs observed in tcpdump samples, though some 1–2s flush delays persisted.
- Prometheus cardinality restored after manual scrape relabel check — confirms that metrics issue was twofold: a relabel bug and the telemetry loss.

Remaining unknowns and follow-ups
- Why did collector start sending TCP RSTs? Check HAProxy/nginx limits at the load balancer layer (do we have a conn-limit baked into front LB?). Check autoscale behavior at that time.
- Confirm agent memory profile: did the agent restarts correlate with OOM or just liveness? journal shows signal but not OOM. Need to capture pprof on a node for a live run.
- Are there any observability-ingest rate-limiting rules (ratelimit service or API gateway) that would proactively RST upstream connections?
- We changed agent defaults in last release (v1.12.0) — reconcile release notes vs. actual deployed config for batch_size and buffer.

Action items (who/what)
- Aisha: collect /var/log/messages and full obs-agent logs for the 17:45–18:10 UTC window and upload to obs-archive bucket. (done: s3://redwood-obs/forensics/2026-02-24/agent-logs.tar.gz)
- Evan: check collector LB (nginx/haproxy) conn limits + recent config changes 2026-02-24 17:00–18:30 UTC.
- Priya: confirm Cilium policy diff and whether rollout was automatic via bootstrap pipeline or manual (PR id?).
- SRE: consider increasing collector connection headroom and add graceful backpressure metrics exposed on collector (queue_depth, accept_failures).
- Product: determine if we should expose a temporary SLO communication to affected customers.

Notes for postmortem draft
- Candidate root cause: combination of agent config regression (smaller buffer/batch) + collector connection saturation triggered by new Cilium egress policy/conn-limits; resulted in RSTs, agent liveness timeouts, and span drops.
- Contributing factors: lack of backpressure metrics on the collector; lack of automated alert on agent buffer fill rate and connection resets; deployment checklist missed validating default agent config on rollout.

Scratch ideas for long-term fixes
- Agent: persist queue to disk for short-term buffering during network blips (configurable fallback).
- Collector: expose accept/conn_reject metrics and configure per-source rate-limits with slow-path queue.
- Platform: add a canary for Cilium policy rollouts that validates egress to telemetry endpoints before mass rollout.
- Testing: load test the collector with synthetic funnel to simulate 600–1200rps sustained and validate tail latencies and conn_count headroom.

Quick links and references
- Collector health endpoint: https://collector.internal/ehealth
- Config map: k8s://observability/configmaps/obs-agent-config
- Agent repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-agent/pull/214
- Cilium policy PR: https://git.internal/cilium/policies/pull/133

Misc notes (random observations recorded during debugging)
- When I temporarily set batch_size to 8, spans were lost faster — confirms buffer batching matters.
- Flushing behavior: agent flush interval currently 5s; with small batch_size high burstiness causes many small flushes which increase connection churn.
- SNI in TLS handshake from node shows collector CN mismatch warning occasionally — file this if we see more TLS errors.

End of scratchpad.
